'''Uruangnirin''' is an [[Austronesian language]] spoken on the islands of Tarak and Faor in the [[Sebakor Bay]], [[West Papua (province)|West Papua]]. Some [[Kalamang|Kalamang people]] from the neighboring island of Karas speak it as a [[second language]].<ref>Visser, Eline. (2016). [http://urn.nb.no/URN:NBN:no-54973 A grammar sketch of Kalamang with a focus on phonetics and phonology]. Master's thesis, University of Oslo.</ref> The languages most closely related to Uruangnirin are [[Onin language|Onin]] and [[Sekar language|Sekar]] of the [[Bomberai Peninsula]].

Uruangnirin is an [[endangered language]] as the younger generations of its speakers are shifting to [[Papuan Malay]], the local [[lingua franca]], as well as [[Indonesian language|Indonesian]], the standard national language.
